About the game

Design it. Fly it. Find out why. Redesign it.

Crimson Atlas is an interactive 3D mission simulator and science story. You are the mission designer and the flight director: every choice you make in the hangar — instruments, solar power, antenna, radiation shielding — changes your delta-v budget and how much science you can bring home. The game then takes you through every stage of a real robotic Mars mission, and ends with a Mission Debrief that traces every result back to the decision that caused it. A clearly labelled what-if bonus chapter about making Mars habitable comes after.

①

Design

Play four roles: Mission Planner, Science Lead, Spacecraft Engineer and Communications. Six live meters show mass, power, budget, data, comms and time. Pick a real launch date and see where Earth and Mars really are. Three difficulty levels change the budget.

②

Fly

Your design is what flies. A small antenna means data waits in the rover and may never reach Earth. A small solar array means the rover stops to recharge. A short plan means the clock runs out.

③

Debrief and refly

The debrief shows plan against result for all six resources and explains each decision. Redesign & Refly keeps your design so you can change one thing and compare attempts.

🛰

Learn by flying it

Trade-offs engineers really face: mass against delta-v, power against distance from the Sun, data against antenna size, landing speed against fuel.

🔬

Do the science

Scan the surface from orbit, choose a landing site, sample soil, read atmosphere and wind, photograph targets and build a mission report.

🌱

Imagine the future

Release the Genesis spores and watch seventy-five years pass: seas fill and forests spread. Phase 1: robots build a city of the next century. Phase 2: the CA-1 ark brings skilled workers, animals and the species that keep life in balance. Phase 3: everyone else.

Mission architecture

One rocket. One mothership. Everything rides together.

A single launch carries the whole mission. Nothing appears from nowhere: every vehicle you fly leaves Earth bolted to the same spacecraft.

1 · The mothership (orbiter)

The spacecraft you design in the hangar. It flies the cruise to Mars, performs the capture burn and stays in orbit for the whole mission.

2 · Three scout satellites

Small satellites carried on the mothership's aft ring. Once in Mars orbit they are released onto different orbits so the whole planet can be mapped quickly.

3 · The lander capsule

Docked on the mothership's nose inside a heat-shield aeroshell. After you choose a site it separates, enters the atmosphere, drops its backshell and heat shield, and lands on its own engine.

4 · Rover and relay

The rover drives out of the lander. The orbiter overhead relays its data back to Earth — the same split of roles real missions such as NASA's Viking orbiter-lander pairs used.

The mission

Six phases you actually play

Each phase has its own camera, live telemetry and a flight director who tells you what is happening and why.

PHASE 01

Hangar: design your mothership

Build the mothership before it ever leaves the ground: an orbiter carrying three scout satellites and the lander capsule. Every instrument adds science and costs delta-v.

  • Fourteen decisions across four roles, six live resource meters
  • Real launch-date planner: try Perseverance's date, or today
  • Too heavy and you will not reach Mars
PHASE 02

Launch from Earth

Roll out to the pad, run the terminal count and ride a two-stage rocket off the planet.

  • Booster separation and second-stage ignition
  • Live altitude, velocity and propellant
PHASE 03

Deep-space cruise

Trans-Mars injection and the long coast between worlds. Look around — the sky is explorable.

  • Find the Sun, Earth, Jupiter and galaxies
  • Mission day, distance and speed telemetry
PHASE 04

Orbit and satellite mapping

Arrive at Mars, release the three scout satellites from the mothership and scan the surface to find where to land.

  • Reconnaissance grid painted in real time over the real NASA Viking map
  • Spectrometer and radar findings reported live
PHASE 05

Entry, descent and landing

The lander capsule separates from the orbiter and dives in. Aeroshell, parachute, heat-shield drop and a controlled retro burn decide everything.

  • Choose a safe or risky, science-rich site
  • Wind, dust devils, Phobos and Deimos overhead
PHASE 06

Rover surface operations

Deploy the rover and do the science you came for.

  • Drive, photograph and scan science beacons
  • Soil sample, habitability lab, atmosphere and wind
Project Genesis · the story chapter · speculative vision

What if Mars could breathe?

After the surface mission, a narrated cinematic shows a fictional seventy-five-year future in three phases: robots first, then CA-1, then everyone else. It is a story about hope, not a forecast — and the game labels it that way on screen.

CHAPTER A

A planet turns green

Genesis spores spread from your landing site. Over seventy years water returns, seas fill and forests climb the hills. The world is alive, but still empty.

  • The whole terrain transforms in front of you
  • Seas, forests, clouds and rain
CHAPTER B · PHASE 1

Robots go first

No people yet. The cargo ship CA-0 lands with robot builders, and they start printing a city from Martian soil.

  • Robots roll down the ramp and get to work
  • Cranes, printers and the first foundations
CHAPTER C · PHASE 1

New Olympus, a city of the next century

By Year +75 the robots have finished New Olympus: curved glass towers with garden rings, sky-bridges, a terraced arcology, floating garden platforms and a space elevator.

  • Flying-car sky-lanes, maglev ring and vertical farms
  • A whole city ready before a single person arrives
CHAPTER D · PHASE 2

Earth, Year +75

Back home the air has turned. Earth is failing. With the city ready, the CA-1 ark is loaded in three sections: skilled workers, animals, and life-balancing species.

  • Narrated city, farmland, forest and coast scenes
  • Boarding on Pad 07
CHAPTER E · PHASE 2

CA-1 lifts off

The ark climbs out of the haze and burns for a Mars that is now blue and green.

  • Three cabin sections and the trans-Mars flight
CHAPTER F · PHASE 2

The doors open

CA-1 lands beside the robot-built city. Workers, then animals, walk down the ramp onto grass under a blue sky.

  • No suits, no masks
PHASE 3 · COMING SOON

Everyone else

The story ends with a message sent back to Earth: “The air is good. Come home.” Arks CA-2 onward are being built for all the people still on Earth.

Science honesty: the mission phases are simplified from how real Mars missions work. The Genesis chapter (spores that green a planet in decades, robot-built cities, open-air breathing on Mars) is fiction and is not established science.
Features

What is inside

 

Spacecraft designer

Camera, spectrometer, radar sounder, solar array size, large antenna and radiation shield — with live science return and delta-v read-outs.

Launch & staging

Countdown, lift-off, booster separation and stage two, with engine plumes, smoke and live altitude and velocity.

Explorable deep space

Drag to look around during cruise: the Sun, Earth, Jupiter, distant galaxies and the Milky Way band.

Orbital mapping

Three satellites lay a glowing scan grid over the real NASA Viking global map of Mars, with nine real NASA landing sites marked.

Skill-based landing

Choose a site, deploy the parachute at the right altitude and hold the retro burn to touch down softly in wind and dust.

Rover operations

Drive the rover, take photos and 360° scans, sample soil, run the habitability lab, and check atmosphere and wind.

Narrated cinematic

Voice narration, music and titles carry the Genesis story from a dying Earth street to a living New Mars.

Upgraded visuals

Filmic tone mapping, image-based reflections, soft shadows, sculpted rocks and layered mesas, a detailed launch complex, normal-mapped water and an HD procedural Mars.

Mission report

Finish with a score and a report of everything you measured, photographed and achieved.

How to play

Controls

On-screen buttons are available for everything, so the game also works on touch screens.

HangarTick the instruments, set the solar array, then press Roll out to launch pad. Keep delta-v above the minimum.
Cruise & orbitDrag look around · Wheel zoom · Double-click reset view
DescentC deploy parachute (below 10 km) · hold Space for the retro burn
RoverW A S D drive · Shift boost · F photo · Q 360° scan · M control room
CinematicUse Voice, Skip scene and Skip all at the top right.
SPACE APPS2026CHALLENGE
Made for

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Crimson Atlas was created as a project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its goal is to make Mars exploration understandable and exciting for students and the public: you learn how a mission is designed, flown and landed by doing it yourself, and you are invited to think about what a long-term human future on Mars could look like.

NASA data used in the game

  • Mars Viking Colorized Global Mosaic (MDIM 2.1), NASA Ames / USGS Astrogeology: the Mars globe you scan from orbit is this real image map. Source
  • Mars24 lander list, NASA GISS: the coordinates of the nine real landing sites marked on the globe (Viking 1 and 2, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, Curiosity, InSight, Perseverance) and the real example given for each landing zone. Source
  • Mars Fact Sheet, NASA NSSDCA: mean surface pressure (6.36 mb) and the atmosphere gas mix (CO₂ 95.1%, N₂ 2.59%, Ar 1.94%, O₂ 0.16%, CO 0.06%) used in the landing and the rover's atmosphere readings. Source
  • Planetary orbital elements, NASA / JPL Solar System Dynamics: the live Earth–Mars distance on this page and in the game's top bar and the launch-date planner (where Earth and Mars are on the date you pick, and whether the launch window is open) are computed from these elements (approximate, within about 0.5%). Source
  • Mars 2020 Perseverance mission pages and landing quick facts, NASA / JPL: reference for the Mission Design Console and the entry, descent and landing sequence. Source

Budget, mass and science scores in the Mission Design Console are simplified game values, and the Genesis chapters are fiction.

MISSION BRIEFING

Welcome Commander. Your objective is to design, launch, and successfully land a scientific probe on Mars.

  • One rocket, one mothership: Your spacecraft is an orbiter that carries three small scout satellites and a lander capsule. At Mars it releases the scouts to map the surface, then drops the lander and stays in orbit as its radio relay.
  • Spacecraft Design: Balance science instruments, power, and shielding against the rocket equation.
  • Interplanetary Cruise: Monitor Delta-V and handle solar radiation safely.
  • Landing Site Selection: Review satellite scan reconnaissance data to pick your landing site carefully.
  • Touchdown: Deploy parachutes below 10 km and fire retro-rockets to survive! Look behind the lander: Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.
  • Surface Operations: Measure gases, wind and storms, take a soil sample, then deploy the rover (W A S D), photograph science targets, run the Habitability Lab (can humans live here?) and watch it all from the live Mission Control room (M).
